name: Poland
tagline: Cheap, big, and more free English-taught places than you think
summary: Polish law makes full-time study in Polish free at public universities for EU citizens, and although English-taught programmes are allowed to charge, some of them do not. At the University of Warsaw an EU citizen pays nothing for English-taught American Studies, English Studies or International Studies in Philosophy, while a non-EU student pays up to 5,500 euros. Your IB Diploma is recognised automatically by Polish law with no nostrification. The thing that will decide your application is not your total points but which subjects you took at Higher Level, because Polish universities convert HL and SL very differently.
whyConsider: An IB Diploma is recognised by operation of law in Poland under article 93 of the Education System Act, with no nostrification and no extra procedure.
Some English-taught bachelor's at the University of Warsaw cost EU citizens nothing at all, while non-EU students pay. The rule is programme by programme, so read the fee schedule.
Full-time Polish-language study at a public university is free for you by statute - if you are willing to learn Polish, tuition disappears entirely.
English-taught engineering is affordable: AGH runs from 2,500 euros a year for Space Engineering to 6,000 for Computer Science, and Wroclaw Tech from about 3,950 to 5,850 euros.
English-taught medicine at Gdansk is around 14,800 euros a year, among the cheapest six-year MD programmes in Central Europe.
The Jagiellonian School of Medicine in English has an explicit Denmark rule: a Danish English grade of 7 satisfies its English requirement.
watchOuts: If you study medicine here and then want to work in Denmark, the diploma alone is not enough. Poland's entry in Annex V of the EU professional qualifications directive requires the LEK state exam certificate, and the Polish medical chamber says it can only certify full qualifications if you also have a recognised postgraduate internship. See the medicine-abroad page before you commit.

HL versus SL matters more than your total. At the Medical University of Gdansk a grade 7 at Standard Level scores 60 points while a 6 at Higher Level scores 86. Poznan University of Medical Sciences requires Biology, Physics or Chemistry at HL.
Poland's maintenance grant and student loan are closed to a Danish student who is not working in Poland, under article 324(3) of the Higher Education Act. Your funding has to come from Denmark.
Every foreign candidate at Wroclaw Tech must sit a compulsory online maths-with-logic entrance exam, whatever your IB Maths grade.
There is no central application portal. Each university runs its own IRK system with its own deadline, fee and exam.

Only Poznan University of Medical Sciences has published a working autumn-2027 calendar. Warsaw and the Jagiellonian have adopted their 2027/28 Senate resolutions, which fix outer bounds - Warsaw may not start before 2 February 2027 and must finish by 30 September, the Jagiellonian must be open by 30 June and closed by 1 October - but in both cases the day-by-day timetable comes later, in a Rector's ordinance expected in January or February 2027. AGH and Wroclaw Tech have published nothing at all for 2027/28.
Karta Polaka is irrelevant to you. It requires Polish ancestry, and EU citizenship already gives you the identical fee exemption for Polish-taught study.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: The University of Warsaw maps Standard Level onto the Polish poziom podstawowy and Higher Level onto poziom rozszerzony. For languages, Ab initio and B SL count as SL, B HL counts as HL, and Language A at either level (and Literature and Performance) counts as bilingual level, which is then converted to extended level by multiplying by 4/3 and capping at 100 per cent. Mathematical Studies SL counts as SL. The Jagiellonian applies a multiplier of 1/2 to Standard Level subjects.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: University of Warsaw (Senate resolution 107 of 21 May 2025, for 2026/27 admissions) converts IB grades to Polish matura percentages: 7 = 100 per cent, 6 = 90, 5 = 75, 4 = 60, 3 = 45, 2 = 30. The Jagiellonian instead multiplies the IB grade by 100/7, so a 7 is 100 per cent and a 5 about 71.4, then halves Standard Level results. The Medical University of Gdansk publishes a two-column table: at HL a 7 scores 100, 6 scores 86, 5 scores 71, 4 scores 57, 3 scores 43 and 2 scores 29; at SL the same grades score 60, 51, 43, 34, 28 and 17.
notes: The legal basis is article 93 of the Education System Act of 7 September 1991. The Ministry of Education states that IB diplomas issued by the International Baccalaureate Organisation in Geneva confirm secondary education in Poland, are recognised by operation of law without any additional procedure, and require no nostrification.
NAWA confirms that a Director's information is not required for IB and EB certificates, so there is no recognition procedure to go through.

One caveat from the Ministry page: automatic recognition of secondary education does not itself settle eligibility to apply for higher education, and applicants are referred to NAWA. The exact NAWA position on the IB for admission purposes could not be read and should be checked.
The University of Warsaw asks IB candidates to supply a document from the school or education authorities stating that the diploma entitles the holder to university study in the country of issue.
No statutory minimum IB point total exists. Thresholds are set programme by programme in each university's admission resolution.
Poznan University of Medical Sciences requires IB candidates to have taken Biology, Physics or Chemistry at Higher Level for medicine.
The practical lesson: choose your HL subjects in the first year of the Diploma to match the programme you want, because that decision outweighs your total score.

portal.name: None nationally. Almost every university runs its own IRK system (Internetowa Rekrutacja Kandydatow) - irk.uw.edu.pl at Warsaw, irk.uj.edu.pl at the Jagiellonian, irk.usos.pwr.edu.pl at Wroclaw Tech, e-Rekrutacja at AGH, applicant.ump.edu.pl at Poznan Medical.

deadlines.notes: Two PUMS pages disagree and neither is usable as printed. The application calendar's "Start of classes" card says "13 Sep 2026" - a 2027 calendar carrying a 2026 day - while the medicine admission requirements page, under a "Fall 2027 entry" heading, says "Start of classes: September 6, 2027". The second cannot be right either, because the same calendar page puts orientation at 6-12 September 2027, and PUMS runs classes after orientation, not during it: for 2026/27 it published orientation 7-13 September and classes 14 September 2026. The reading the evidence supports is Monday 13 September 2027 - orientation Monday to Sunday, classes the following Monday - but that string appears on no PUMS page, so no date is recorded here. Neither page carries a last-updated stamp, so there is no way to tell which figure is the stale one. This one needs an e-mail to the admissions office.

steps: Decide first whether you are going the English-taught route or are willing to learn Polish. Full-time Polish-language study at a public university is free to you by law, and that is the biggest single financial lever available.
Read each university's fee schedule programme by programme. Do not assume English-taught means you pay - at the University of Warsaw several English-taught bachelor's are free for EU citizens.
Register on each university's own IRK portal. There is no shared application, so budget for several application fees of 85-150 PLN each, plus 600 PLN if you sit the Poznan medical exam.
Work out how your HL and SL grades convert at each target university. The three published tables - Warsaw, Jagiellonian and Gdansk - give very different answers.
Book any entrance exam. Medical exams at Gdansk, Poznan and the Jagiellonian are online; Wroclaw Tech's compulsory maths exam is online through its ePortal.
Upload your IB diploma when results arrive. The University of Warsaw explicitly allows IB candidates to register first and add results by mid-July.
Once admitted, apply for a dormitory place immediately - the Jagiellonian allocates on a rolling basis as places become available, with no guarantee.
After you arrive, register your stay at the voivodeship office if you will be in Poland more than three months. This is a legal obligation under article 20 of the 2006 EU movement act.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is set per programme by each university's admission resolution, usually by converting your IB grades to Polish matura percentages and ranking candidates. Medicine is different: the Jagiellonian School of Medicine in English admits solely on the entrance examination result, Poznan requires a mandatory 60-question natural sciences test plus a 20-40 minute oral, and Gdansk sets a written biology and chemistry paper plus a roughly 20-minute Zoom interview. Wroclaw Tech requires every foreign candidate to sit an online mathematics-with-logic exam of about ten open tasks in 90 minutes. Several Jagiellonian English-taught programmes involve an interview while others have none.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Substantial and spread across many universities. Wroclaw Tech alone states 33 programmes fully taught in English across bachelor's and master's. The University of Warsaw prices at least 11 English-taught bachelor and long-cycle programmes, AGH lists 7 English-taught bachelor's, and the Jagiellonian lists 7 plus a joint bachelor plus medicine and dentistry in English. A reliable national total could not be verified.
language.englishProof: An IB Diploma taught and examined in English is normally enough. The University of Warsaw's admission resolution states explicitly that an IB diploma proves English at B2 or above where English was the language of instruction and examination, so no IELTS is needed. The Jagiellonian lists the International Baccalaureate Diploma as an accepted document confirming B2 English. Where a test is required instead: University of Warsaw accepts IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, PTE Academic 59 or Cambridge B2 First and above; the Jagiellonian School of Medicine wants IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 87; Poznan University of Medical Sciences sets the highest bar found at IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 94, PTE Academic 60 or Cambridge Advanced.
notes: The Jagiellonian School of Medicine in English publishes a Denmark-specific rule: a Danish school English grade of 7 satisfies its English requirement, alongside Norway 4, Sweden C, Finland 5 and Iceland 8.
Poznan University of Medical Sciences does not list the IB diploma as English proof, so budget for an IELTS sitting if you target PUMS.
If you take the free Polish-taught route, the University of Warsaw accepts an IB or EB diploma showing a result in Polish as proof of Polish.
Medicine taught in English still means clinical work with Polish-speaking patients, so Polish is taught alongside.

tuitionEuEea.value: Free for full-time Polish-language study at a public university, by statute. For English-taught programmes it depends on the programme. University of Warsaw 2026/27: American Studies, English Studies and International Studies in Philosophy are free of charge for EU/EFTA/Swiss citizens; Archaeology 2,300 EUR; Business and Management 4,000 EUR; European Politics and Economics, International Relations, Political Science and Social and Public Policy 4,300 EUR each; Finance, International Investment and Accounting 4,200 EUR; Psychology (long-cycle) 25,200 PLN, about 5,800 EUR. AGH 2026/27 per year: Space Engineering 2,500 EUR, Geology of Natural Resources and Mechanical Engineering 3,450 EUR, Mechatronic Engineering 3,600 EUR, Computer Physics 4,000 EUR, Computer Science for Embedded Systems 5,000 EUR, Computer Science 6,000 EUR. Wroclaw Tech 2026/27 per year: Management 17,200 PLN (about 3,960 EUR), Electronic and Computer Engineering 17,600 PLN, Applied Computer Science 17,800 PLN, Mechanical Engineering 18,600 PLN, Medical Informatics 25,400 PLN (about 5,840 EUR). English-taught medicine: Medical University of Gdansk 64,200 PLN a year, about 14,770 EUR, for the six-year MD (2026/27); Poznan University of Medical Sciences 71,000 PLN a year in years 1-2 and 85,750 PLN in years 3-6, about 16,340 and 19,730 EUR, totalling 485,000 PLN or about 111,600 EUR.

tuitionNonEu.value: At the University of Warsaw the gap is real and large: American Studies 5,500 EUR, English Studies 2,200 EUR and International Studies in Philosophy 1,500 EUR for non-EU students against free for EU citizens, and Psychology 27,600 PLN against 25,200. At AGH, Wroclaw Tech, the Medical University of Gdansk and Poznan University of Medical Sciences the published schedules print a single price for everyone, so EU citizenship buys no discount on those English-taught programmes. The national portal quotes an average of about 2,000 EUR a year for first, second and long-cycle studies for fee-paying foreigners, 2,000-6,000 EUR across public and private institutions, and 8,000-12,000 EUR for MBAs.

costs.applicationFee: University of Warsaw 85 PLN, or 100 PLN if the programme has a written or oral exam or interview. Jagiellonian 85 PLN without an exam and 100 PLN with one for 2026/27; its School of Medicine in English lists 100 PLN marked as to be confirmed. Wroclaw Tech 100 PLN, or 150 PLN for Architecture. Poznan University of Medical Sciences 85 PLN processing plus a 600 PLN exam and interview fee. Medical University of Gdansk 100 PLN registration. At the National Bank of Poland reference rate of 22 September 2026 (1 EUR = 4.3463 PLN), 85 PLN is about 20 EUR and 600 PLN about 138 EUR.

livingCostMonthly.value: Roughly 450-800 EUR a month all in, for a student living in a dormitory in Warsaw or Krakow. The official national portal says 1,500-2,000 PLN a month, which it converts to 330-430 EUR, but that page states no year and its dormitory figure of 400-600 PLN is contradicted by verified 2026/27 dormitory rates of 670-1,270 PLN at the Jagiellonian. At the September 2026 exchange rate, 1,500-2,000 PLN is 345-460 EUR.
livingCostMonthly.year: Portal figures undated and apparently stale; dormitory figures verified for 2026/27

notes: The official portal's component figures, re-converted at the September 2026 rate: groceries 700-900 PLN (about 160-207 EUR), public transport 50-60 PLN, entertainment 150-200 PLN, health insurance 40-60 PLN, phone and internet 80-100 PLN.

Poznan University of Medical Sciences, whose page is dated 2026/27, puts a student month at 800-1,600 US dollars, with accommodation 200-850, food 150-300, a 25 dollar monthly transport pass and 20 dollars of insurance.

Gdansk charges a separate Orientation Week fee of 3,100 PLN, reduced to 2,050 PLN for candidates from Poland and premedical course graduates. Its medical tuition is paid in instalments due 15 October and 15 February.
Poznan asks for a 4,800 PLN down payment on the acceptance e-mail, with year one payable in four instalments.
All euro conversions here use the National Bank of Poland reference rate of 22 September 2026: 1 EUR = 4.3463 PLN.
No 2027/28 tuition figures were published anywhere as of September 2026.

funding: The strongest financial move is structural: full-time study in Polish at a public university is free to an EU citizen under article 324(2)(1) of the Higher Education Act, and the University of Warsaw accepts an IB diploma showing a Polish result as proof of Polish.
The second strongest is to check the English-taught fee schedule programme by programme. Several University of Warsaw English-taught bachelor's cost EU citizens nothing.

Be clear about what you cannot get. Article 324(3) restricts the Polish maintenance grant (stypendium socjalne) and the Polish student loan (kredyt studencki) to EU citizens who are workers, self-employed, retain a right of residence on that basis, or hold permanent residence. A Danish student who simply arrives to study cannot claim either.
A rector can waive or reduce fees by administrative decision under article 324(1), and the minister or the NAWA director can do so for NAWA scholarship holders. It is worth asking.

NAWA runs three incoming-student programmes - the gen. Anders Programme, Poland My First Choice, and the Banach Scholarship Programme - but their eligibility rules could not be read. The gen. Anders programme is by name and design aimed at people of Polish descent and Banach at developing countries, so do not assume a Danish student qualifies for any of them without reading the call document.
Erasmus+, CEEPUS and the Visegrad Scholarship Programme are listed on the national portal as options once you are enrolled.

Whether the rector's merit scholarship (stypendium rektora) is open to EU citizens is not settled here. Article 324(3) restricts only the maintenance grant and the loan, which implies the merit scholarship is not restricted, but no source was found stating that outright.
Danish SU and Danish tuition support are decided in Denmark at su.dk and ufm.dk. Apply early.
workRights: As an EU citizen you need no work permit. Article 16(1) of the 2006 act on entry and residence of EU citizens treats being a worker or self-employed person in Poland as an independent ground of residence, with no funds or insurance test attached. An explicit official page stating that EU students need no permit, and whether any hour limits apply to students, could not be verified. Working also matters for money reasons beyond the wage: taking up work is what unlocks the Polish maintenance grant and student loan, which are otherwise closed to you. Source: https://lexlege.pb.pl/ustawa-o-wjezdzie-na-terytorium-rzeczypospolitej-polskiej-pobycie-oraz-wyjezdzie-z-tego-terytorium-obywateli-panstw-czlonkowskich-unii-europejskiej-i-czlonkow-ich-rodzin/art-16/
residency: For the first three months you need do nothing beyond holding a valid travel or identity document, under article 15 of the 2006 act on entry and residence of EU citizens. Beyond three months you have a right of residence as a student under article 16(3) provided you have sufficient funds not to become a burden on social assistance and you have health insurance - and the article expressly accepts entitlement under EU social security coordination, which is the EHIC route, so your Danish blue card satisfies it. Article 20(1) then obliges you to register your residence, which you do at the voivodeship office for where you live. The national portal says EU students should apply for registration within 90 days of arrival and are issued a cost-free certificate of registration. The detailed procedure, forms and processing time could not be verified. Sources: https://study.gov.pl/visa-application and https://lexlege.pb.pl/ustawa-o-wjezdzie-na-terytorium-rzeczypospolitej-polskiej-pobycie-oraz-wyjezdzie-z-tego-terytorium-obywateli-panstw-czlonkowskich-unii-europejskiej-i-czlonkow-ich-rodzin/art-20/
housing: Jagiellonian University dormitory rates for 2026/27 are published and there is no higher rate for foreign students: a place in a multi-person room is 670 PLN a month (about 154 EUR) in the standard houses and 850 PLN in Bursa Raclawicka; a single room is 870 or 1,070 PLN; sole occupancy of a double is 1,200 or 1,225 PLN; a studio-type single at Bursa Raclawicka is 1,270 PLN (about 292 EUR). Places are allocated on a rolling basis as they become available, so a room is not guaranteed - apply the moment you are offered one. Poznan University of Medical Sciences charges 820-1,500 PLN a month depending on room and building, and estimates private renting at up to four times the dormitory cost. Public universities are expressly permitted to charge for dormitories and canteens under article 79(2)(6) of the Higher Education Act, separately from tuition. University of Warsaw dormitory rates could not be verified. Sources: https://akademiki.uj.edu.pl/ds/oplaty and https://pums.edu.pl/admissions/student-accommodation/
healthcare: As an EU citizen you use your Danish European Health Insurance Card. The national portal states that a valid passport, student identity card and a valid EHIC entitle the holder to medical care free of charge in Poland. Polish residence law also expressly accepts entitlement under EU coordination rules as satisfying the health insurance condition for a student's right of residence. Two cautions: an EHIC is designed for medically necessary treatment during a temporary stay rather than as long-term cover for a resident student, and Polish universities commonly expect either voluntary National Health Fund (NFZ) insurance or private cover. Non-EU students sign a voluntary NFZ agreement costing about 15 EUR a month. The NFZ premium and enrolment route for an EU student could not be verified. Source: https://study.gov.pl/health-insurance

institutions.name: University of Warsaw
institutions.englishBachelors: At least 11 English-taught bachelor and long-cycle programmes in the official 2026/27 fee schedule: American Studies, Archaeology, Business and Management, English Studies, European Politics and Economics, Finance International Investment and Accounting, International Relations, International Studies in Philosophy, Political Science, Psychology (long-cycle) and Social and Public Policy
institutions.note: Poland's largest university and the only one found that gives EU citizens free tuition on several English-taught bachelor's while charging non-EU students - and it publishes the clearest official IB conversion table in the country.

institutions.name: Jagiellonian University
institutions.englishBachelors: 7 English-taught first-cycle programmes - Earth Sciences in a Changing World, East European Studies, European Studies, Global and Development Studies, International Relations and Area Studies, Mathematics and Computer Science Advanced Track, Responsible Entrepreneurship and Management - plus the Una Europa Joint Bachelor in Sustainability and the School of Medicine in English
institutions.note: Poland's oldest university, founded in 1364, and one of the few with its 2027/28 admission rules already adopted - its medical school also publishes a Denmark-specific English requirement.

institutions.name: Warsaw University of Technology
institutions.note: One of Poland's leading institutes of technology and among the largest universities in Central Europe, with 19 faculties - but its English-taught programme list, fees and deadlines could not be verified and must be requested directly.

institutions.name: AGH University of Krakow
institutions.englishBachelors: 7 English-taught bachelor's: Computer Physics, Computer Science, Computer Science for Embedded Systems, Geology of Natural Resources, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronic Engineering and Space Engineering
institutions.note: The widest set of clearly priced English-taught engineering bachelor's found in Poland, running from 2,500 euros a year for Space Engineering to 6,000 for Computer Science.

institutions.name: Kozminski University
institutions.note: A private non-profit business school named after the economist Leon Kozminski, which also hosts the Central and Eastern European campus of ESCP - its programme list, fees and deadlines could not be verified.

institutions.name: SGH Warsaw School of Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught first-cycle programmes exist and there is an entrance exam, but the programme names, count and fee amounts could not be verified
institutions.note: Poland's oldest economics university, founded in 1906 as August Zielinski's Private Trade Courses, and its flagship public business school - it sets an entrance exam for international applicants.

institutions.name: Wroclaw University of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: 33 programmes fully taught in English across bachelor's and master's, out of 62 bachelor's and 57 master's programmes in total. Verified English-taught bachelor's with 2026/27 prices: Applied Computer Science, Management, Mechanical Engineering, Medical Informatics and Electronic and Computer Engineering
institutions.note: The one thing to know before applying: every foreign candidate must sit a compulsory online mathematics-with-logic entrance exam, whatever their IB Maths grade.

institutions.name: Poznan University of Medical Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught six-year MD and Dentistry, plus a Medical Summer Program
institutions.note: The only Polish institution found with a fully published autumn-2027 application calendar, and it explicitly requires IB candidates to have taken Biology, Physics or Chemistry at Higher Level.

institutions.name: Medical University of Gdansk
institutions.englishBachelors: Four English-taught programmes plus a preparatory year: the six-year Doctor of Medicine, five-year Master of Pharmacy, three-year Bachelor of Nursing, a two-year International Master in Sustainable Drug Discovery, and a one-year Premedical Course
institutions.note: The cheapest verified English-taught MD in Poland at about 14,770 euros a year for 2026/27, and it publishes the clearest IB Higher Level versus Standard Level points table of any Polish university.

institutions.name: Medical University of Warsaw
institutions.englishBachelors: An English Division exists, but its programme list, fees and deadlines could not be verified - the admissions host returned errors throughout
institutions.note: One of the oldest and largest medical schools in Poland, tracing to the first academic department of medicine in 1809 - but you will have to get fee and deadline information directly from the university.

institutions.name: Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan
institutions.note: Traditionally ranked among Poland's most reputable universities and the main general-academic option in Poznan, though its English-taught offer and fees could not be verified.

institutions.name: University of Wroclaw
institutions.note: The largest higher-education institution in Lower Silesia, with over 100,000 graduates since 1945 - fees and English-taught programme count unverified.

institutions.name: Poznan University of Technology
institutions.note: Described as one of the best technical universities in Poland and a non-capital alternative to Warsaw and Wroclaw, though its English-taught offer and fees could not be verified.

notCheckedNotes: Apart from Poznan University of Medical Sciences, and the statutory outer bounds in the Warsaw and Jagiellonian 2027/28 Senate resolutions, no Polish institution had published autumn-2027 deadlines as of September 2026. Every other date here is 2026-entry and carries provisional: true.

The Poznan University of Medical Sciences class-start contradiction is checked but not closed. The application calendar prints 13 September 2026 under "Start of classes" on a Fall 2027 calendar; the admission requirements page prints 6 September 2027, which collides with the same calendar's orientation week of 6-12 September 2027. The 2026/27 pattern (orientation 7-13 September, classes 14 September) points to Monday 13 September 2027, but no PUMS page prints that, so the record carries no date. Only the admissions office can settle it.

The University of Warsaw result-upload extension for IB and EB candidates - the single most IB-specific deadline in Poland - has no 2027 date. The 2026/27 dates were 14 July and 14 September 2026. The 2027 equivalents live in a Rector's ordinance not yet issued; the 2026/27 one appeared on 20 January 2026.

The Jagiellonian's 2027/28 medical-certificate deadline is not dated. Annex 1 to Senate resolution 62/V/2026 keeps the requirement but says only "w wyznaczonym terminie", leaving the day to the Rector's ordinance. The 2026 pattern was 28 August for Collegium Medicum and 7 September for everything else.
Jagiellonian School of Medicine in English tuition, and Jagiellonian English-taught non-medical bachelor fees, could not be read on any page.
Medical University of Warsaw English Division tuition, deadlines, entrance exam format and programme list are unverified - the admissions host returned errors throughout.
SGH fee amounts, programme names and admissions schedule, and Kozminski's programme list, tuition and deadlines, are unverified.
Warsaw University of Technology, Adam Mickiewicz University, University of Wroclaw and Poznan University of Technology could not be verified for fees, English-taught programme counts or deadlines.

Whether seven of the University of Warsaw's English-taught programmes print a single flat price or conceal an EU/non-EU split was not resolved - the extracted table showed one figure spanning both columns. Re-read the PDF before relying on those rows.
The exact NAWA position on the IB for admission (as distinct from recognition of secondary education) could not be read and is the most important open question here.
The academic year of the Medical University of Gdansk IB conversion table is not printed on the page.
Whether Gdansk or Poznan exempt IB holders from their entrance exams, and whether either sets a minimum IB grade, is not stated anywhere.
No art, design, music or architecture academy was researched, and entrance requirements for those fields in Poland are unverified.
Eligibility, amounts and deadlines for the three NAWA scholarship programmes could not be read, so whether a Danish student with no Polish ancestry qualifies for any of them is unknown.
Whether the rector's merit scholarship is open to EU citizens is implied but not stated by any source read.
The practical residence-registration procedure for EU citizens - which office, form, processing time and fee - could not be verified; only the statutory obligation is.
No official page was found stating explicitly that EU citizens need no work permit in Poland, nor any student hour limits.
The NFZ voluntary insurance premium for a student and the enrolment route for an EU citizen are unverified.

Founding years for Warsaw University of Technology, Medical University of Gdansk, Adam Mickiewicz University, University of Wroclaw and Poznan University of Technology could not be verified and are left blank.

An amendment to article 79 of the Higher Education Act (Dz.U. 2025.0.1837) takes effect on 1 January 2027. On the text seen it does not disturb the tuition rule, but it should be re-checked before autumn 2027.
